india_context: India has the highest TB burden globally — 26% of world TB cases. Fully curable with proper treatment.
diagnosis: Sputum test (CBNAAT/GeneXpert), chest X-ray, Mantoux test. FREE testing at government DOTS centres.
treatment: DOTS (Directly Observed Therapy Short-course) — 6 months. COMPLETELY FREE under NIKSHAY programme by Government of India. Do NOT stop treatment early.
prevention: BCG vaccine at birth. Ventilation. Nutrition. Early diagnosis and treatment of cases.
government_scheme: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana — TB patients get Rs 500/month nutritional support

india_context: Common in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Northeast India, tribal areas. Two main types: P.vivax (common) and P.falciparum (dangerous).
symptoms: cyclical fever every 48-72 hours with chills, sweating, shaking
in severe cases: jaundice, confusion, dark urine
diagnosis: Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) — available at government PHCs FREE. Blood smear microscopy.
treatment: P.vivax: Chloroquine + Primaquine (14 days). P.falciparum: Artemisinin Combination Therapy (ACT). PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED. FREE at government health centres.
prevention: Sleep under insecticide-treated nets. Eliminate standing water. Mosquito repellent. Indoor residual spraying.
emergency_signs: Any fever with confusion, seizures, inability to walk, severe breathing difficulty = P.falciparum severe malaria — emergency
government_scheme: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme — FREE diagnosis and treatment

india_context: Very common in India due to contaminated water and food. Particularly high in monsoon season.
symptoms: constipation more common than diarrhoea in adults
diagnosis: Widal test (screening), Blood culture (gold standard), TYPHIDOT rapid test.
treatment: Azithromycin 500mg once daily 7 days OR Ciprofloxacin. PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED. Rest and fluids essential. Monitor for complications: intestinal perforation (severe abdominal pain = emergency).
prevention: Typhoid vaccine (Vi polysaccharide — 3 years protection, conjugate vaccine — longer). Safe water — boil or purify. Avoid street food. Hand hygiene.
critical_warning: Severe abdominal pain in typhoid patient = possible intestinal perforation = EMERGENCY — go to hospital immediately

india_context: Epidemic seasons: post-monsoon (August-November). Common in Delhi, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala. Urban Aedes aegypti mosquito bites during daytime.
symptoms: severe joint and muscle pain (break-bone fever)
treatment: NO specific antiviral. Paracetamol ONLY for fever — NEVER Ibuprofen or Aspirin. Oral hydration. Platelet monitoring. Hospitalise if warning signs or platelet below 100,000.
prevention: Eliminate stagnant water. Use repellents. Full sleeve clothing. Mosquito nets. Awareness.
critical_rule: NEVER give Ibuprofen, Aspirin, or NSAIDs in suspected dengue — causes dangerous bleeding

india_context: Common in India, spread by same Aedes mosquito as dengue. Major outbreaks occur every few years.
symptoms: severe joint pain especially in hands feet wrists ankles (can persist months)
diagnosis: CHIKV IgM antibody test after day 5.
treatment: No specific treatment. Paracetamol or Ibuprofen for pain (SAFE to use unlike dengue). Rest. Fluids. Joint pain may persist for months.
prevention: Same as dengue — mosquito control measures.

india_context: Common during and after floods. Walking in waterlogged areas. Maharashtra, Kerala, Tamil Nadu coastal areas.
diagnosis: Leptospira IgM ELISA, blood culture. Clinical diagnosis during flood season.
treatment: Doxycycline 100mg twice daily 7 days (mild). Penicillin G or Ampicillin IV for severe. PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED.
prevention: Avoid wading in flood water. Boots and gloves if unavoidable. Doxycycline prophylaxis during flood exposure (prescription).
high_risk: Farmers, sewer workers, flood rescue workers, veterinarians

india_context: Most common nutritional deficiency in India. Affects 53% of women and 50% of children. Major cause: poor diet, parasitic infections, frequent pregnancies.
symptoms: pica (craving non-food items like mud, chalk)
diagnosis: CBC: Hb below 12 (women) or 13 (men). Serum Ferritin (most sensitive). MCV below 80 (microcytic).
treatment: Iron supplements: Ferrous Sulphate 200mg or Ferrous Fumarate twice daily with Vitamin C. Take on empty stomach if tolerated. Continue 3 months after Hb normalises.
diet: Increase: spinach, lentils, beans, dates, jaggery, meat, fish. Take with Vitamin C (lemon, orange). Avoid tea/coffee with iron-rich meals.
government_scheme: Anaemia Mukt Bharat programme — FREE iron-folic acid supplements at government facilities and ASHA workers

india_context: 1 in 4 adults in India has hypertension. Only 12% have it under control. Major cause of stroke, heart attack, kidney failure.
silent_killer: Usually NO symptoms until complications. Many Indians first discover hypertension after a stroke or heart attack.
risk_factors_india: High salt diet (pickles, papads, processed food)
treatment: Lifestyle first: low salt less than 5g/day, DASH diet, exercise 30 min/day, no tobacco, weight loss. Medications if BP above 140/90 consistently: Amlodipine, Telmisartan, Atenolol (PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED).
monitoring: Home BP monitoring: Check morning before medicines. Target below 130/80 for most. Below 140/90 minimum.
government_scheme: Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres offer FREE BP screening and basic medicines
